description: Reviewed join between the committed NumPy-oracle contracts and coverage catalog row ids, read by coverage/oracle_evidence.py. Every entry is validated on each run: target ids must exist in the catalog, explicit entries must be used, must not merely repeat what the automatic rules already resolve, and aliases must point at a row with direct contracts and must not shadow one. A corpus op key that neither the automatic rules nor this table resolve fails the generator.

bare_key_precedence.note: A key without a dot names a top-level API. The FIRST existing callable/property row wins, so np.* shadows its np.linalg / np.random namesakes: the corpus keys trace/diagonal/outer/cross/vecdot/tensordot/matmul/matrix_transpose call np.<name> (gen_oracle.py) and power calls np.power; the np.linalg Array-API forms are credited only through the reviewed aliases below, never by name. Rows whose kind is class/constant/module are skipped here (np.fft is a module; fft resolves to np.fft.fft) and can only be targeted by an explicit key entry.

prefix_rules.note: A dotted key <head>.<rest> names a namespaced API. The first existing row among the head's templates wins; the numsharp.* fallback resolves NumSharp-only members the corpus gates (e.g. chebyshev.chebvalnd, NumSharp's N-D evaluation twin).

files_without_op.note: Corpus files whose schema predates the common op field. Their rows replay under the named key.

matrix.note: np.matrix(data, dtype, copy): the constructor over arrays of every rank, matrices, literals and Python sequences. The catalog row of the class; the key carries no member name.

set_default_printstyle.note: numpy.polynomial.set_default_printstyle(style) (polyprint tier): the class flag ABCPolyBase._use_unicode after the call, over styles of every kind (the two accepted texts, near misses, Python numbers / None / lists / tuples, NumPy scalars, arrays: the truth value of their comparison with a str), or NumPy's ValueError. A key of the numpy.polynomial package itself, which no prefix rule names (polynomial.* is numpy.polynomial.polynomial).

average_returned.note: np.average(..., returned=True); NumSharp spells the tuple-returning form average_returned.

byteswap.note: a.byteswap() - an ndarray method keyed without the ndarray. prefix.

clip_out.note: Aliasing tier: np.clip with out= aliasing an input.

put_selfvals.note: Aliasing tier: np.put whose values are a view of the target (PyArray_PutTo copies the target first, so every value is the original's), raise / wrap / clip.

put_selfidx.note: Aliasing tier: np.put whose indices are a view of an integer target (the same copy makes every index the original's), raise / wrap / clip.

clip_pyint.note: np.clip with Python-int bounds: _methods._clip's drop rule, NEP 50 OverflowError packing, dtype=/out= casts named after the routed ufunc.

clip_ufunc.note: np.clip as the ufunc call it routes to: broadcast array bounds, out= (up-broadcast, layouts, casts, read-only, shape), where=, out overlapping an input, the const-vs-general float loop choice, broadcast and keyword-rule error texts.

reduce_kwargs.note: Reductions through their NumPy-shaped overload: out= (dtypes, strided / F views, keepdims), where= (every broadcast form, Python bools, 0-d), every axis form, and NumPy's reduce-prologue errors in NumPy's order (read-only out, the mask dtype, the axis, out's rank, the reduction iterator's shape checks).

minmax_kwargs.note: The max / min family with NumPy's keywords (params.fn: max / min / amax / amin / nanmax / nanmin / ndarray.max / ndarray.min): out= of every dtype pairing and layout (the loop is promote_types(out, a), a cast out round-trips at every buffer fill), initial= of every kind into every loop dtype, where= (every broadcast form, Python bools), the float bits of NumPy's iterator calls (±0 ties, NaN payloads), np.setbufsize fills, the fresh result's layout, and NumPy's errors in NumPy's order.

axis_arg.note: The axis arguments of every axis-taking function (params.fn: the NumPy spelling - sum / ndarray.argmax / ma.sum / linalg.norm / fft.fft - across the np.* functions, the ndarray methods, numpy.ma, np.linalg and np.fft): every axis value of a 0-d to 3-D operand in range and out of it, repeated / out-of-range / empty / full tuples (a repeat together with an out-of-range axis in both orders), the two-axis functions one axis at a time, a dtype sweep of the out-of-range axes, masked numpy.ma operands, and the stacking family's empty operand list; NumPy's result, or its AxisError / ValueError / IndexError type and text (normalize_axis_index's msg_prefix, PyArray_CheckAxis' rank 1 for a 0-d operand, normalize_axis_tuple's repeat texts, the IndexError of a.shape[axis]).

copyto_full.note: np.copyto as NumPy's array_copyto: where= masks of every layout, sources of every layout and rank (leading unit axes stripped), every dtype through the masked copy, casts, overlapping views (NumPy's temporary or its raw 1-D order), C# literal sources (NumPy's weak Python scalars), 0-d and empty arrays, and NumPy's errors in NumPy's order; each case compares the destination's whole buffer.

weak_scalar.note: NEP 50 weak Python scalars given as C# literals (params.fn: the six comparisons, add / subtract / multiply / maximum / minimum / fmax / fmin / bitwise_and / bitwise_or / bitwise_xor / floor_divide / remainder / fmod / power / gcd / left_shift / right_shift / arctan2 / hypot / copysign / heaviside / logaddexp, clip): the comparison at the array's precision with the scalar packed into it (an int through the double, a complex as complex64 against float16 / float32), exact Python-int comparisons for integer arrays, every route (np.*, both C# operator overloads, out=, where=, iterator layouts), int64 / uint64 literals past 2^53 packed into float32 loops, a weak Python int range-checked against an integer loop (NumPy's OverflowError, in NumPy's order before power's negative-exponent error), and empty operands broadcast through np.* and the operators. Section S STORES the literal (params.fn: setitem_* = ndarray.__setitem__ through the integer / negative / slice / empty / ellipsis / fancy / mask routes, attached to ndarray.__setitem__'s row (generator 1.14.0) as the index oracle's set is; fill = ndarray.fill; flat_index / flat_slice = the flat iterator; full, full_like, put, putmask, place, put_along_axis, insert, fill_diagonal, pad, asarray, copyto = numpy.{value}): a Python scalar is PyArray_Pack'ed on every route (range-checked, never wrapped; an int past 2^53 rounds twice into float16 / float32), a NumPy scalar (C# Half / char) is int()-converted into a signed integer on the PyArray_Pack routes and cast on the PyArray_FromAny routes.

arange_full.note: np.arange as NumPy's PyArray_ArangeObj: the length from Python's arithmetic on the bounds (float and Python-int bounds, the underflow and divide-by-inf counts, the 2**63 boundary), start and start + step stored into the dtype, the rest filled in the dtype's own arithmetic (float ramps, float16 in float32, integer ramps that wrap, fractional steps into integer dtypes), and NumPy's errors in its order.

power_fast.note: np.power / np.float_power (params.fn) over NumPy's float power loops: the scalar-exponent fast path (1/x, 1, sqrt, x, x*x) exactly where NumPy's inner-loop calls see the exponent with step 0 (0-d, one-element, (1,1), stride-0 broadcast and varying exponents, casts the trivial loop copies or the iterator buffers, np.setbufsize thresholds), every base layout, out= / where= / dtype=, float16's powf, float_power's plain pow, and power's errors; an out case compares the out's whole buffer.

dtype.note: np.dtype(string) descriptor construction, and np.dtype(scalar class): a concrete class's descriptor, NumPy's TypeError text for each abstract class.

sctype.note: NumPy's scalar classes (params.cls: the ten abstract classes np.generic ... np.character, the classes NumSharp has no dtype for np.complex64 / np.object_ / np.void, and the concrete classes reached as np.dtype(spec).type): __name__ / __qualname__ / __module__ / repr / __mro__ / __bases__ / __base__ / mro() / __subclasses__() as qualified names (Python's built-in bases included), isinstance of a NumPy scalar of every dtype and of an array, issubclass of every class. The datetime classes have no NumSharp np.* member of their own, and Python's built-in classes (params.cls 'py:float', ...) are no NumPy API, so their contracts attach to no row.

typecodes.note: np.typecodes: each group's type-code string and the key order.

sctypeDict.note: np.sctypeDict: the dtype each name's scalar class converts to, for every name whose class NumSharp has.

True_.note: np.True_: NumPy's bool scalar True (a C# bool).

False_.note: np.False_: NumPy's bool scalar False (a C# bool).

longdouble.note: np.longdouble: the descriptor np.dtype(np.longdouble) is (float64 on win-amd64, the platform the corpus is generated on), and np.issubdtype(np.float64, np.longdouble) is False (a class of its own).

ScalarType.note: np.ScalarType: its length and the membership of every scalar class the section names (the order lists intc or longlong by the C long model, so it is pinned by the unit tests instead).

flatten.note: a.flatten() - an ndarray method keyed without the ndarray. prefix.

get.note: Advanced-indexing oracle: ndarray.__getitem__ (a[index] over every index kind). The protocol has its own row since coverage generator 1.14.0; until then the contracts attached to the ndarray type.

set.note: Advanced-indexing oracle: ndarray.__setitem__ (a[index] = value), its own row as for get.

grnd.note: PCG64 Generator streams (np.random.default_rng(seed).<method>); random_integers and rs_bytes replay the legacy RandomState helpers on a fresh seeded RandomState.

indices_sparse.note: np.indices(..., sparse=True); NumSharp spells the tuple-returning form indices_sparse.

ma.flatten.note: NumPy m.flatten() replayed through NumSharp's np.ma.flatten(m).

ma.fill.note: ma_fill tier: call-history scripts over a masked array's fill value as NumPy stores it - the constructor's conversion and TypeErrors, the getter's materialized default, the setter writing into a stored fill (also through ma.set_fill_value), inheritance by every derive kind (shared through _update_from, a converted copy through __array_finalize__ in astype / view / byteswap), filled(), the repr's fill_value= line, common_fill_value.

ma.masked_array.note: NumPy's ma.masked_array IS the MaskedArray class, catalogued under both spellings; NumSharp exposes the constructor as np.ma.masked_array, which credits the numpy.ma.masked_array row.

maximum_out.note: Aliasing tier: np.maximum with out= aliasing an input.

minimum_out.note: Aliasing tier: np.minimum with out= aliasing an input.

ndarray.note: np.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer, offset, strides, order): the ndarray type's constructor (ndarray.__new__), gated by ndarray_ctor.jsonl. The catalog row is the class, which the namespace rules skip.

nditer_construct.note: Construction tier: cast checks, copy / updateifcopy routes, the 0-d auto copy, the common dtype, NumPy's per-operand check order, and the advance-on-entry protocol; per operand the value stream, the operand after construction and the array after close.

nditer_protocol.note: State-contract tier: scripted traces of pulls, seeks, range resets, remove_axis / remove_multi_index / enable_external_loop, element reads and it[i] = v writes, copies and close (the started / finished flags, NumPy's texts), the tracked index through ordering, flips and coalescing, and op_axes reductions (unbuffered).

nditer_ranged.note: A ranged, buffered cast iteration over [start, end): the buffers refill at the range start.

nditer_values.note: Error contract: iterating a zero-size operand without zerosize_ok.

nonzero_all.note: Every output array of np.nonzero at any rank.

out_binary.note: Binary ufunc out=/where= tier (the ufunc name rides in params.ufunc).

random_api.note: Random-API oracle (gen_random_oracle.py): every overload of the random world by exact C# signature; params.member is <Owner>.<member> (a constructor is the class name alone). RandomState members also credit the np.random module function (the global RandomState's bound method); Generator members do not (the same-named module functions are the legacy ones). BitGenerator's members invoked on an engine also credit the BitGenerator row. Members without a catalog row map to nothing. Rebuilt by test/oracle/random_api_oracle_map.py.

rnd.note: Legacy MT19937 streams: np.random.seed(s); np.random.<dist>(...). The module-level function IS the global RandomState's bound method, so both rows share the contracts.

round_.note: np.round(a, decimals); NumPy 2 removed np.round_, NumSharp keeps the spelling.

viewflags.note: The array-object oracle (gen_viewflags_oracle.py, view_flags.jsonl): the object each API returns (params.fn) -- a view, a copy, the operand itself, or a fresh array -- and its memory facet (C / F / OWNDATA / WRITEABLE / ALIGNED flags, byte strides, shares-memory and identity per operand; for a tuple which slots share memory or are one object) over 21 source layouts. getitem is ndarray.__getitem__ (its own row since coverage generator 1.14.0, as the index oracle's get is); where1 / where3 are np.where's one- and three-argument forms.

outflags.note: The out= object oracle (gen_viewflags_oracle.py, out_flags.jsonl): f(..., out=o) over every out-capable API (params.fn: every ufunc, the reductions and scans, the products, the FFT family, the ndarray methods) with out arrays of six layouts (C / F owners, an offset view, a stepped view, a transposed view, a reversed view): the returned object must BE o (identity), the slots of o's whole base buffer the call did not write keep their prior contents, and a refused out is NumPy's verbatim error. The FFT names map to np.fft (the bare fft would hit the module row).

shapearg.note: The shape-argument oracle (gen_viewflags_oracle.py, shape_args.jsonl): every shape-taking API (params.fn) called with the same dims in each C# form (Shape, long[], int[], int, and a view's Shape of every view layout -- the class of the view-Shape allocation overrun), recording the result's values and memory facet and NumPy's refusals of invalid dims; indices_sparse is np.indices(sparse=True).

aliases.note: Rows with no direct contracts whose NumSharp member is a reviewed pure delegation of a row that has them. Mirrors test/NumSharp.Tests.Oracle/Fuzz/OracleSurfaceCoverageTests.cs (EquivalentAliases, NdarrayAliases, MaAliases) plus the np.linalg Array-API forms that delegate verbatim in BOTH NumPy (numpy/linalg/_linalg.py) and NumSharp (LinearAlgebra/linalg/np.linalg.arrayapi.cs). np.linalg.trace/diagonal/outer/cross are NOT here: their contracts differ from the np.* forms (last-two axes, 1-D and 3-vector validation).

numpy.polynomial.Chebyshev.reason: numpy.polynomial.Chebyshev is the class numpy.polynomial re-exports from numpy.polynomial.chebyshev; NumSharp's np.polynomial.Chebyshev(coef, domain, window, symbol) is new NDChebyshev(coef, domain, window, symbol).

numpy.polynomial.Legendre.reason: numpy.polynomial.Legendre is the class numpy.polynomial re-exports from numpy.polynomial.legendre; NumSharp's np.polynomial.Legendre(coef, domain, window, symbol) is new NDLegendre(coef, domain, window, symbol).

numpy.polynomial.Laguerre.reason: numpy.polynomial.Laguerre is the class numpy.polynomial re-exports from numpy.polynomial.laguerre; NumSharp's np.polynomial.Laguerre(coef, domain, window, symbol) is new NDLaguerre(coef, domain, window, symbol).

numpy.polynomial.Hermite.reason: numpy.polynomial.Hermite is the class numpy.polynomial re-exports from numpy.polynomial.hermite; NumSharp's np.polynomial.Hermite(coef, domain, window, symbol) is new NDHermite(coef, domain, window, symbol).

numpy.polynomial.HermiteE.reason: numpy.polynomial.HermiteE is the class numpy.polynomial re-exports from numpy.polynomial.hermite_e; NumSharp's np.polynomial.HermiteE(coef, domain, window, symbol) is new NDHermiteE(coef, domain, window, symbol).

numpy.row_stack.reason: NumPy 2.x row_stack is vstack plus a DeprecationWarning; NumSharp credits it to np.vstack.

numpy.linalg.matmul.reason: np.linalg.matmul(x1, x2) is _core_matmul in NumPy and np.matmul in NumSharp.

numpy.linalg.tensordot.reason: np.linalg.tensordot delegates to np.tensordot in both libraries.

numpy.linalg.matrix_transpose.reason: np.linalg.matrix_transpose delegates to np.matrix_transpose in both libraries.

host_pins.note: Tiers that are hard-gated only on the pinned host and Inconclusive elsewhere, beyond the RunHostLibmCorpus(...) tiers oracle_evidence.py discovers from FuzzCorpusTests*.cs by itself.

matmul_parity.jsonl.reason: Byte parity through NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS; strict only when the content-hash-pinned scipy-openblas loads (matmul_parity.host.jsonl).

linalg_parity.jsonl.reason: LAPACK factorisations through NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS at threads=1; strict only on the pinned library (linalg_parity.host.jsonl).

polyalgebra_parity.jsonl.reason: numpy.polynomial series algebra (U2) whose np.convolve reaches OpenBLAS's vector ?dot kernels; byte parity through NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS's ISlidingDotBackend at threads=1, strict only on the pinned library (polyalgebra_parity.host.jsonl).

polyroots_parity.jsonl.reason: numpy.polynomial {p}roots (U7) that run LAPACK geev through NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS at threads=1; strict only on the pinned library (polyroots_parity.host.jsonl).

npy.note: test/NumSharp.Tests/IO/corpus/npy_oracle.zip (real np.save / np.savez output), replayed by NpyOracleTests. Variant = case kind, suffixed :compressed for savez_compressed archives and :load_npy for the typed-reader cases. The NEP 55 StringDType kinds (NumPy pickles such an array behind the descr '|O'): tpickle = a .npy file written and read with allow_pickle, tpickle_raw = a bare pickle np.load unpickles, tnpz = an archive with a StringDType member.

flags.note: test/NumSharp.Tests/Backends/corpus/flags_oracle.jsonl, replayed by FlagsOracleTests. Variant = read (flags of a recipe) or setflags (after setflags write/align/uic ops).

strings.note: test/NumSharp.Tests.Oracle/Strings/corpus/strings_<section>.jsonl (the string oracle), replayed by StringOracleTests; only its numpy.strings calls are joined (oracle_evidence.STRINGS_OPS). Variant = str_fn:<name> for the str_fn op (params.name is the numpy.strings function: the search, strip, pad, replace, partition, slice, comparison, predicate, case, translate, mod and codec sections over S / U / StringDType), strings_add for np.strings.add and strings_multiply for np.strings.multiply (with an integer or a text count).
